description: In mta_sts_policy.rs parse_mta_sts_policy(), line 47: 'let (key, value) = match line.split_once(": ") { Some(pair) => pair, None => continue }'. The idiomatic Rust 1.65+ form is: 'let Some((key, value)) = line.split_once(": ") else { continue };'. let-else reads linearly (early exit on the else branch) and avoids the inner binding (pair => pair). The current form is not wrong but is the pre-1.65 idiom.
title: Policy parser split_once match should use let-else
